And a fire shall burn continually upon the altar; it shall not be quenched.
This is the law of the sacrifice which the sons of Aaron shall bring before the Lord, opposite the altar.

And he shall take a handful from the fine flour of the sacrifice, with its oil and the frankincense upon the sacrifice, and offer it up upon the altar as an offering: a sweet savour, its memorial portion unto the Lord.
But Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it unto them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; it is most holy, as the offering for sin and the guilt offering.
Every male among the priests shall eat it; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations, from the offerings of the Lord. Whosoever touches them shall be sanctified.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

This is the gift of Aaron and his sons which they shall bring unto the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour as a continual sacrifice, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It shall be made upon a griddle with oil; he shall bring it mixed, in rolled pieces, a sacrifice of fragments, a sacrifice for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his stead shall prepare it. It is an everlasting law; it shall all be fully performed.
And every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burned, and shall not be eaten.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

Speak unto Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the offerings for sin before the Lord; they are most holy.
The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
Whosoever touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and if any of its blood is sprinkled upon a garment, what it was sprinkled upon shall be washed in a holy place.
And the earthenware vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water.
Every male among the priests shall eat them; they are most holy unto the Lord.
And none of the offerings for sin whose blood is brought into the Tent of Testimony to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten; they shall be burned with fire.
And this is the law of the ram for the guilt offering; it is most holy.
In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord; and he shall pour the blood round about upon the base of the altar.
And he shall bring all its fat from it: the loin, and all the fat which covers the inward parts, and all the fat upon the inward parts,
and the two kidneys, and the fat upon them which is by the thighs, and the lobe upon the liver; these he shall remove with the kidneys.
And the priest shall offer them up upon the altar as an offering unto the Lord. It is for guilt.
Every male among the priests shall eat them; they shall eat them in a holy place. They are most holy.
As the offering for sin, so also the guilt offering: one law is theirs. It shall belong unto the priest who makes atonement with it.
And the priest who brings a man’s whole burnt offering shall have the hide of the whole burnt offering which he brings.
And every sacrifice made in an oven, and every sacrifice made upon a hearth or upon a griddle, shall belong unto the priest who brings it.
And every sacrifice prepared with oil, or not so prepared, shall belong unto all the sons of Aaron, unto each an equal share.
This is the law of the sacrifice of deliverance which they shall bring unto the Lord.
If he brings it for praise, he shall bring with the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour prepared with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil.
He shall bring his gifts with leavened loaves, with a sacrifice of praise and deliverance.
And he shall bring one of all his gifts as a portion set apart unto the Lord; it shall belong unto the priest who pours the blood of the offering of deliverance.
And the flesh of the sacrifice of praise and deliverance shall be his, and shall be eaten on the day when it is given; they shall leave none of it until morning.
And if he sacrifices his gift as a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day when he brings his sacrifice, and on the morrow.
And what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire.

But if he eats any of the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for him who brings it, neither shall it be reckoned unto him; it is a defilement. And the soul that eats of it shall bear the sin.
And flesh which touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Whosoever is clean shall eat flesh.
But the soul that eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall perish from among his people.

And if a soul touches any unclean thing, human uncleanness, or unclean four-footed beasts, or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, that soul shall perish from among his people.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: You shall eat no fat of cattle, or sheep, or goats.
And fat from animals that have died, or from those torn by wild beasts, may be used for any work; but it shall in no wise be eaten as food.
Whosoever eats fat from the livestock from which an offering is brought unto the Lord, that soul shall perish from among his people.
You shall eat no blood in any dwelling place of yours, whether of birds or of livestock.
Every soul that eats blood, that soul shall perish from among his people.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,
And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: He who brings a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord shall bring his gift unto the Lord from the sacrifice of deliverance.
His hands shall bring the offerings unto the Lord: the fat upon the breast and the lobe of the liver; he shall bring them to place them as a gift before the Lord.
And the priest shall offer up the fat upon the altar; and the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.
And the right foreleg you shall give as a portion set apart unto the priest from your sacrifices of deliverance.
He among the sons of Aaron who brings the blood of the offering of deliverance and the fat shall have the right foreleg as his portion.

For the breast of the presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart have I taken from the sons of Israel, from your sacrifices of deliverance; and I have given them unto Aaron the priest and unto his sons as an everlasting statute from the sons of Israel.
This is Aaron’s anointing and the anointing of his sons from the offerings of the Lord, on the day when he brought them forward to serve as priests unto the Lord,
as the Lord commanded to be given them from the sons of Israel on the day when he anointed them: an everlasting statute throughout their generations.
This is the law of the whole burnt offerings, and the sacrifice, and the offering for sin, and the guilt offering, and the consecration, and the sacrifice of deliverance,
as the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day when He commanded the sons of Israel to bring their gifts before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses did as the Lord directed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses said unto the congregation: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

And he clothed him with the tunic, girded him with the belt, clothed him with the under-robe, and put the shoulder-piece on him. He girded him according to the shoulder-piece’s workmanship and fastened him securely in it.
And he placed the oracle-piece on it and put Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece.
And he put the turban on his head and placed on its front the gold plate, the consecrated holy object, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses took some of the anointing oil,

and sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with belts, and put turbans on them, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the calf for the sin offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the calf of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and put it with his finger all around on the altar’s horns, cleansing the altar. He poured out the blood at the altar’s base and consecrated it, to make atonement upon it.
And Moses took all the fat on the inward parts, the lobe on the liver, both kidneys and the fat on them, and Moses offered them up on the altar.
And he burned up the calf, its hide, its flesh, and its dung with fire outside the camp, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses brought the ram for the whole burnt offering forward, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he divided the ram limb by limb, and Moses offered up the head, the limbs, and the fat.
And he washed the belly and feet with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar: a whole burnt offering for a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Moses brought the second ram forward, a ram of consecration, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it upon Aaron’s right earlobe, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.

And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on their right earlobes, the extremities of their right hands, and the extremities of their right feet. Moses poured the blood all around against the altar.
And he took the fat, the loin, the fat on the belly, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the right foreleg.
And from the basket of consecration before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat and the right foreleg.
And he put everything on Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands and offered them up as a portion set apart before the Lord.
And Moses took them from their hands, and Moses offered them up on the altar upon the whole burnt offering of consecration, which is a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord.
And Moses took the breast and removed it as a presentation before the Lord from the ram of consecration. It became Moses’ portion, as the Lord commanded Moses.

And Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him. He consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

And Moses said unto Aaron and his sons: Boil the flesh in the court of the Tent of Testimony, in a holy place, and there you shall eat it, and the loaves in the basket of consecration, as I have been directed, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them.
And what remains of the flesh and loaves shall be burned up with fire.
And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, until the day is fulfilled, the day of your consecration; for he shall consecrate your hands for seven days.
As he has done this day, the Lord commanded it to be done, to make atonement for you.
And you shall remain at the door of the Tent of Testimony seven days, day and night; you shall keep the charges of the Lord, so that you do not die, for thus the Lord God commanded me.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things the Lord directed Moses.
And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.
And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.
And speak unto the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male young goat from the goats for sin, and a calf and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a whole offering,
and a calf and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.
And they brought what Moses commanded opposite the Tent of Testimony, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the Lord.
And Moses said: Do this thing which the Lord said, and the glory of the Lord shall appear among you.

And Moses said unto Aaron: Draw near unto the altar, and prepare your offering for sin and your whole burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your house; and prepare the gifts of the people, and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And Aaron drew near unto the altar and slaughtered the calf for the sin offering.
And Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him. He dipped his finger in the blood, put it on the altar’s horns, and poured the blood at the altar’s base.
And he offered up the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver of the sin offering on the altar, as the Lord commanded Moses.
And he burned up the flesh and hide with fire outside the camp.
And he slaughtered the whole burnt offering. Aaron’s sons brought him the blood, and he poured it all around against the altar.
And they brought him the whole burnt offering limb by limb, the parts and the head, and he placed them on the altar.
And he washed the belly and feet with water and placed them upon the whole burnt offering on the altar.
And they presented the gift of the people; and he took the male young goat for the sin offering of the people, and slaughtered it as the first.
And he presented the whole burnt offering and prepared it as was fitting.
And he presented the sacrifice, filled his hands with some of it, and placed it on the altar, apart from the morning whole burnt offering.
And he slaughtered the calf and ram of the people’s sacrifice of deliverance. Aaron’s sons brought him the blood, and he poured it all around against the altar.
And as for the fat from the calf and ram—the loin, the fat covering the belly, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the lobe on the liver—
he placed the fat upon the breasts; and they offered up the fat upon the altar.
And Aaron removed the breast and the right foreleg as a portion set apart before the Lord, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Aaron lifted his hands over the people and blessed them. He came down after preparing the offering for sin, the whole burnt offerings, and the deliverance offerings.
And Moses and Aaron entered the Tent of Testimony. They came out and blessed all the people, and the Lord’s glory appeared to all the people.
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed what was on the altar, both the whole burnt offerings and the fat. All the people saw, were astonished, and fell on their faces.
And the two sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, each took his firepan, and put fire upon it, and placed incense upon it, and presented strange fire before the Lord, which the Lord had not commanded them.
And fire came out from the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.

And Moses said unto Aaron: This is what the Lord said, saying: Among those who draw near unto Me I will be sanctified, and in the whole congregation I will be glorified. And Aaron was deeply stricken.

And Moses called Misadai and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, sons of the brother of Aaron’s father, and said unto them: Draw near, and carry your brethren away from before the holy things, outside the camp.
And they came near and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, as Moses had said.

And Moses said unto Aaron, and unto Eleazar and Ithamar his remaining sons: You shall not remove your turbans, neither shall you rend your garments, lest you die and wrath come upon the whole congregation. Your brethren, the whole house of Israel, shall weep over the burning by which they were burned by the Lord.
And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Testimony, lest you die; for the anointing oil from the Lord is upon you. And they did according to the word of Moses.
And the Lord spoke unto Aaron, saying:

You shall drink no wine or strong drink, you and your sons with you, when you enter the Tent of Testimony, or when you approach the altar, so that you do not die: an everlasting statute throughout your generations,
to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

And Moses said unto Aaron, and unto Eleazar and Ithamar, the remaining sons of Aaron: Take the sacrifice which remains from the offerings of the Lord, and eat it unleavened beside the altar; it is most holy.
And you shall eat it in a holy place; for this is your prescribed portion and the prescribed portion of your sons from the offerings of the Lord, for thus I have been commanded.

And you shall eat the breast of the separated portion and the foreleg of the portion set apart in a holy place, you and your sons and your house with you; for it was given as your prescribed portion and the prescribed portion of your sons from the sacrifices of deliverance of the sons of Israel.

They shall bring the foreleg of the portion set apart and the breast of the separated portion with the offerings of fat, to set apart a separated portion before the Lord; and it shall be an everlasting prescribed portion for you, and for your sons and your daughters with you, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses diligently sought the male young goat for the sin offering, and, behold, it had been burned. And Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the remaining sons of Aaron, saying:

Why did you not eat the offering for sin in a holy place? For it is most holy; He gave it unto you to eat, that you might take away the sin of the congregation and make atonement for them before the Lord.
For none of its blood was brought into the holy place. You shall eat it in front, within, in a holy place, as the Lord directed me.

And Aaron spoke unto Moses, saying: If this day they have presented their offerings for sin and their whole burnt offerings before the Lord, and these things have befallen me, shall I eat the offerings for sin this day? Would it be acceptable unto the Lord?
And Moses heard, and it pleased him.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
Every animal among the livestock that divides the hoof, and cleaves its claws into two hoofs, and brings up the cud: these you may eat.

Nevertheless, of these you shall not eat: among those that bring up the cud and those that divide the hoof and cleave the claws, the camel, because it brings up the cud, but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean unto you;
and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you;
and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you.
You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat.
And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination.
And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses.
And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle;
and the vulture, the kite, and those like it;
and the raven and those like it;
and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it;
and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis;
and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan;
and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you.
But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth.
And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it.
Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile;
the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole.
These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered.
And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean.
And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you.
But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean.
But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whosoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.

And whosoever eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.

And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you.
And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them;

for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
for I am the Lord who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God; and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord.
This is the law concerning animals, birds, every creature that moves in the water, and every creature that creeps upon the earth,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that are eaten and the living creatures that are not eaten.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a woman receives seed and bears a male, she shall be unclean seven days; she shall be unclean as in the days of separation for her menstrual discharge.
And on the eighth day he shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
But if she bears a female, she shall be unclean twice seven days according to her menstrual discharge; and she shall remain sixty-six days in her unclean blood.

And when the days of her purification for a son or daughter are completed, she shall bring unto the priest at the door of the Tent of Testimony an unblemished year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for sin.
And the priest shall present it before the Lord, and make atonement for her, and cleanse her from the fountain of her blood. This is the law for her that bears a male or a female.

If her hand cannot provide enough for a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a whole burnt offering and one for sin. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
If anyone has on the skin of his body a bright scar-like mark, and it becomes a lesion of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.
If the bright spot on his skin is white but does not appear lower than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, but it is faint, the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the lesion remains before him, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for a second seven days.

And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day a second time; and, behold, if the lesion is faint, and the lesion has not shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is a mark; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the mark changes and shifts in the skin after the priest has examined him for cleansing, he shall appear before the priest a second time,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the mark has shifted in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy.
And when a lesion of leprosy occurs in anyone, he shall come unto the priest.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there is a white scar in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is some sound living flesh in the scar,
it is longstanding leprosy on the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out abundantly in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to foot, throughout the whole view of the priest,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare him clean as to the lesion, because it has all turned white; it is clean.
And on whatever day living skin appears on him, he shall be defiled.
And the priest shall examine the sound skin, and the sound skin shall make him unclean, because it is unclean; it is leprosy.
But if the sound skin is restored and turns white, he shall come unto the priest,
and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the lesion clean; he is clean.
And if an ulcer occurs on the skin of the body and heals,
and a white scar or a whitish or fiery-red bright spot appears in the place of the ulcer, he shall appear before the priest.

And the priest shall examine it; and, behold, if its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin of the body, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
If it spreads in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy that has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the bright spot stays in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the ulcer; the priest shall declare him clean.
And if the skin of the body has a burn from fire, and the healed area of the burn on his skin becomes a shining, bright, whitish-red or completely white spot,

the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the hair in the shining spot has turned white, and its appearance is lower than the skin, it is leprosy which has blossomed in the burn; and the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it, and, behold, there is no white hair in the shining spot, and it is not lower than the skin, but is faint, the priest shall isolate him seven days.
And the priest shall examine him on the seventh day; but if it has indeed spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a lesion of leprosy which has blossomed in the ulcer.
But if the shining spot stays in its place, has not spread in the skin, and is faint, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, for it is the mark of the burn.
And if a man or woman has a lesion of leprosy on the head or beard,

the priest shall examine the lesion; and, behold, if its appearance is more hollow than the skin, and there is fine yellowish hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a broken patch, leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.

And if the priest examines the lesion of the broken patch, and, behold, its appearance is not more hollow than the skin, and there is no yellowish hair in it, the priest shall isolate the lesion of the broken patch seven days.

And the priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread, and there is no yellowish hair in it, and the appearance of the broken patch is not hollow below the skin,
then the skin shall be shaved, but the broken patch shall not be shaved. The priest shall isolate the broken patch for a second seven days.

And the priest shall examine the broken patch on the seventh day; and, behold, if the broken patch has not spread in the skin after he was shaved, and its appearance is not hollow below the skin, the priest shall declare him clean; and having washed his garments, he shall be clean.
But if the broken patch has indeed spread in the skin after he has been cleansed,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the broken patch has spread in the skin, the priest shall not inspect for yellow hair, for he is unclean.
But if before him the broken patch has remained in place and black hair has grown in it, the broken patch has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
And if a man or woman has shining, whitish patches on the skin of the body,
the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if there are shining, whitish patches on the skin of his body, it is a white eruption; he is clean. It blossoms in the skin of his body; he is clean.
If anyone loses the hair of his head, he is bald; he is clean.
If he loses the hair at the front of his head, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
But if there is a white or fiery-red lesion on his bald head or bald forehead, it is leprosy on his bald head or bald forehead.
And the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the appearance of the lesion on his bald head or his bald forehead is white tinged with red, like the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body,
he is a man with leprosy; the priest shall surely declare him unclean; his lesion is upon his head.
And he that has leprosy, in whom the lesion is, shall have his garments loosened and his head uncovered, and shall put a covering about his mouth, and shall be called unclean;
all the days in which the lesion is upon him, being unclean, he shall be unclean; he shall dwell apart; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
And if a garment has a lesion of leprosy, whether a woollen garment or a garment of coarse flax,
or in warp or weft, or in linen or wool, or in leather or any worked leather,
and the lesion in the leather, garment, warp, weft, or any worked leather article is greenish or fiery red, it is a lesion of leprosy, and he shall show it unto the priest.
And the priest shall examine the lesion, and the priest shall isolate the lesion for seven days.

And on the seventh day the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has spread in the garment, warp, weft, or leather, in whatever use is made of leather, the lesion is persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
He shall burn up the garment, the warp or weft in wool or linen, or any leather article that has the lesion, for it is persistent leprosy; it shall be burned up with fire.
But if the priest examines it and the lesion has not spread in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article,
then the priest shall give instructions, and he shall wash the article with the lesion; the priest shall isolate the lesion for a second seven days.

And after it has been washed, the priest shall examine the lesion. If it has not changed its appearance and has not spread, it is unclean; it shall be burned up with fire. It has become established in the garment, warp, or weft.
And if the priest examines it and the lesion is faint after washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, leather, warp, or weft.
If it appears again in the garment, warp, weft, or any leather article, it is blossoming leprosy; the affected article shall be burned up with fire.
And a garment, warp, weft, or any leather article that is washed, from which the lesion departs, shall be washed a second time and be clean.
This is the law of a lesion of leprosy in a garment of wool or coarse flax, or in warp or weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
This is the law of the person with leprosy on the day he is cleansed: he shall be brought unto the priest,
and the priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall examine him; and, behold, if the lesion of leprosy has healed in him that had leprosy,
then the priest shall give orders, and they shall take two living clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop for the person who has been cleansed.
And the priest shall give orders, and they shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water.
And he shall take the living bird, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the living water.
And he shall sprinkle the person cleansed from leprosy seven times, and he shall be clean. He shall release the living bird into the plain.

And the person who has been cleansed shall wash his garments, shave off all his hair, bathe in water, and be clean. Afterward he shall enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his house for seven days.
And on the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, and his eyebrows; he shall shave off all his hair. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished year-old lambs, one unblemished year-old sheep, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one kotyle of oil,
and the priest who performs the cleansing shall present the person being cleansed and these things before the Lord at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall take one lamb and present it for the guilt offering, with the kotyle of oil, and separate it as a separated portion before the Lord.

And they shall slaughter the lamb in a holy place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin. The offering for sin is like the guilt offering: it belongs unto the priest; it is most holy.
And the priest shall take some of the guilt offering’s blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.
And the priest shall take some of the kotyle of oil and pour it upon the priest’s left hand,
and dip his right finger into the oil on his left hand and sprinkle with his finger seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put the oil remaining in his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
The priest shall put the remaining oil in his hand on the head of the person who has been cleansed. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
And the priest shall prepare the offering for sin and make atonement for the unclean person being cleansed from his sin. Afterward the priest shall slaughter the whole burnt offering.
And the priest shall offer up the whole burnt offering and sacrifice on the altar before the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be cleansed.

If he is poor and his hand cannot provide, he shall take one lamb for his offence as a portion set apart, to make atonement for him, a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one kotyle of oil,
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever his hand can provide, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.
And on the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing unto the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord.
And the priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the kotyle of oil, and place them as a presentation before the Lord.

And he shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering. The priest shall take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot.
And the priest shall pour some of the oil upon the priest’s left hand,
and with his right finger the priest shall sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

And the priest shall put some of the oil on his hand on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, the extremity of his right hand, and the extremity of his right foot, on the place of the guilt offering’s blood.
He shall put the remaining oil in the priest’s hand on the head of the person who has been cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
And he shall prepare one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, as his hand can provide,
one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering, together with the sacrifice. The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person being cleansed.
This is the law for the one with a lesion of leprosy and for the one whose hand cannot provide for his cleansing.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
When you enter the land of the Canaanites, which I give unto you for a possession, and I put a lesion of leprosy in the houses of the land of your possession,
then the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, saying: Something like a lesion has appeared to me in the house.
And the priest shall command that the house be emptied before he enters to examine the lesion, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Afterward the priest shall enter to examine the house.
And he shall examine the lesion in the walls of the house, greenish or fiery-red hollows whose appearance is lower than the walls,
and the priest shall leave the house, go to its door, and isolate the house for seven days.
And the priest shall return on the seventh day, and examine the house; and, behold, if the lesion has not spread in the walls of the house,
then the priest shall command them to remove the stones that have the lesion and throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
And they shall scrape the house all around inside and pour the dust outside the city into an unclean place.
And they shall take other scraped stones and put them in place of those stones. They shall take other earth and plaster the house.
If a lesion comes again and springs up in the house after the stones have been removed and the house scraped and plastered,
then the priest shall enter and examine it. If the lesion has spread in the house, it is persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
And they shall demolish the house, and carry its timbers, its stones, and all its dust outside the city into an unclean place.
And whosoever enters the house during any of the days it is isolated shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever sleeps in the house shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening, and whosoever eats in the house shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.

But if the priest comes and enters and examines it, and, behold, the lesion has not spread at all in the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, for the lesion has healed.
And to purify the house he shall take two living clean birds, cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop.
And he shall slaughter one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water,
and take the cedarwood, spun scarlet thread, hyssop, and living bird, dip it in the blood of the bird slaughtered over living water, and sprinkle the house with them seven times,
and he shall purify the house with the bird’s blood, the living water, the living bird, the cedarwood, the hyssop, and the spun scarlet thread.
And he shall release the living bird outside the city into the plain, make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
This is the law concerning every lesion of leprosy and every broken patch,
and for leprosy of a garment or house,
and for a scar, a mark, or a shining spot,
and to explain on what day it is unclean and on what day it shall be cleansed. This is the law of leprosy.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses and Aaron, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If any man has a flow from his body, his flow is unclean.

And this is the law of his uncleanness: discharging seed from his body through the flow by which his body has become stopped up, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the flow of his body, in which his body has become stopped up through the flow, are his uncleanness.
Every bed on which the man with a seminal discharge lies is unclean, and every article on which the man with a seminal discharge sits shall be unclean.
And whosoever touches his bed shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever sits on an article on which the man with a seminal discharge has sat shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches the skin of the man with a seminal discharge shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
If the man with a seminal discharge spits on someone clean, that person shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And any donkey saddle on which the man with a seminal discharge mounts shall be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening. Whosoever carries those things shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
And anyone whom the man with a seminal discharge touches when he has not washed his hands shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
And an earthenware vessel touched by the man with a seminal discharge shall be shattered, and a wooden vessel shall be washed with water and be clean.
When the man with a seminal discharge is cleansed from his flow, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be clean.
And on the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, bring them before the Lord to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and give them unto the priest.
And the priest shall prepare them, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his flow.
And if a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
And every garment and every skin on which there is semen shall be washed with water and be unclean until evening.
And if a man lies with a woman with an emission of semen, they shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
And if a woman has a flow of blood, her flow shall be in her body; she shall remain in her menstrual discharge for seven days. Whosoever touches her shall be unclean until evening,
and everything on which she lies during her menstrual discharge shall be unclean, and everything on which she sits shall be unclean.
And whosoever touches her bed shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
And whosoever touches any article on which she sits shall wash his garments, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
If, while she is on her bed or on the article on which she sits, he touches her, he shall be unclean until evening.
If anyone lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.

And if a woman has a flow of blood for many days outside the time of her menstrual discharge, or if she also has a flow after her menstrual discharge, all the days of her unclean flow shall be like the days of her menstrual discharge; she shall be unclean.

And every bed on which she lies during all the days of her flow shall be like the bed of her menstrual discharge, and every article on which she sits shall be unclean, as in the uncleanness of her menstrual discharge.
Whosoever touches her shall be unclean. He shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and be unclean until evening.
When she is cleansed from her flow, she shall count seven days, and afterward she shall be cleansed.
And on the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them unto the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for her unclean flow.
And you shall make the sons of Israel wary of their uncleannesses, so that they do not die because of their uncleanness in defiling My tent which is among them.
This is the law for the man with a seminal discharge and for anyone who has an emission of semen and becomes defiled through it,
and for the woman bleeding in her menstrual discharge, for the one with a seminal discharge in his flow, male or female, and for the man who lies with a woman in menstrual separation.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses after Aaron’s two sons died when they presented strange fire before the Lord and died.

And the Lord said unto Moses: Speak unto Aaron your brother, and let him not enter at all times into the holy place within the veil, before the propitiatory cover which is upon the ark of testimony, so that he does not die; for I will appear in a cloud above the propitiatory cover.
In this way Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a calf from the cattle for sin and a ram for a whole burnt offering.

And he shall put on a consecrated linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his skin, gird himself with a linen belt, and put on a linen turban. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.
And from the congregation of the sons of Israel he shall take two male young goats from the goats for sin and one ram for a whole burnt offering.
And Aaron shall present the calf for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his house.
And he shall take the two male young goats and present them before the Lord beside the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And Aaron shall place upon the two male young goats one lot for the Lord and one lot for the one sent away.
And Aaron shall present the male young goat on which the lot for the Lord fell and offer it for sin.

And he shall present alive before the Lord the male young goat on which the lot of the one sent away fell, to make atonement over it, so as to send it away for removal. He shall release it into the wilderness.
And Aaron shall present the calf for the sin offering of himself and his house alone, make atonement for himself and his house, and slaughter the calf for his own sin offering.
And he shall take the firepan full of burning coals from the altar opposite the Lord, fill his hands with finely compounded incense, and bring them within the veil,
and put the incense on the fire before the Lord. The vapour of incense shall cover the propitiatory cover above the testimonies, and he shall not die.

And he shall take some of the calf’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the propitiatory cover toward the east; before the propitiatory cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

And he shall slaughter the male young goat for the people’s sin offering before the Lord and bring some of its blood within the veil. He shall do with its blood as he did with the calf’s blood, sprinkling its blood on the propitiatory cover, before the propitiatory cover,

and make atonement for the holy place from the sons of Israel’s uncleannesses and their wrongdoings, concerning all their sins. He shall do the same for the Tent of Testimony established among them amid their uncleanness.

And no one shall be in the Tent of Testimony when he enters to make atonement in the holy place until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself, his house, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.

And he shall go out unto the altar opposite the Lord and make atonement upon it. He shall take some of the calf’s blood and some of the male young goat’s blood and put it all around on the altar’s horns,
and he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleanse it, and consecrate it from the sons of Israel’s uncleannesses.
And he shall finish making atonement for the holy place, the Tent of Testimony, and the altar, and perform cleansing for the priests. He shall present the living male young goat.

And Aaron shall lay his hands on the living male young goat’s head and confess over it all the sons of Israel’s lawless deeds, all their injustices, and all their sins. He shall put them on the living male young goat’s head and send it into the wilderness by the hand of a prepared man.
And the male young goat shall take upon itself their injustices to an inaccessible land, and he shall release the male young goat into the wilderness.
And Aaron shall enter the Tent of Testimony, take off the linen robe he wore when entering the holy place, and lay it aside there.

And he shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his robe. He shall go out, prepare his whole offering and the people’s whole offering, and make atonement for himself, his house, and the people, as for the priests.
And he shall offer up the fat of the offerings for sins on the altar.
And the one who sends away the male young goat designated for release shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water. Afterward he shall enter the camp.

And they shall carry outside the camp the calf and male young goat for the sin offering whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place. They shall burn them up with fire, their hides, flesh, and dung.
The one who burns them shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp.

And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, humble your souls, and you shall do no work, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who is attached unto you.
For on this day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord; and you shall be cleansed.
It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths, a rest unto you; and you shall humble your souls: an everlasting statute.
The priest whom they anoint and whose hands they consecrate to serve as priest after his father shall make atonement. He shall put on the linen robe, a holy robe,
and he shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies, and for the Tent of Testimony and the altar shall he make atonement; and for the priests and for the whole congregation shall he make atonement.
And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make atonement for the sons of Israel from all their sins; it shall be done once in the year, as the Lord directed Moses.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: This is the word which the Lord commanded, saying:
Any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who slaughters a calf, sheep, or goat in the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, to prepare it as a whole burnt offering or an offering of deliverance acceptable unto the Lord for a sweet savour; and whosoever slaughters outside, and does not bring it unto the door of the Tent of Testimony, so as not to present a gift unto the Lord before the tent of the Lord: blood shall be reckoned unto that man; he has poured out blood; that soul shall be destroyed from among his people.

This is so that the sons of Israel may bring up their sacrifices, which they themselves slaughter in the plains; they shall bring them unto the Lord, to the doors of the Tent of Testimony, unto the priest, and sacrifice them as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord.
And the priest shall pour the blood all around against the altar before the Lord beside the doors of the Tent of Testimony and offer up the fat for a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the vain things after which they prostitute themselves. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
And you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who prepares a whole burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Testimony to offer it unto the Lord, that person shall be destroyed from among his people.
And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the resident foreigners attached unto you, who eats any blood: I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and destroy him from among his people.
For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it unto you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the life.
Therefore I have said unto the sons of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood; and the resident foreigner attached unto you shall not eat blood.
And any person of the sons of Israel or of the resident foreigners attached to you who hunts a wild animal or bird that may be eaten shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.
For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said unto the sons of Israel: You shall eat no blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whosoever eats it shall be destroyed.

And every soul, whether among the natives or among the resident foreigners, that eats an animal which has died or has been taken by wild beasts, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening, and shall be clean.
But if he does not wash his garments and does not bathe his body in water, he shall bear his lawless deed.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: I am the Lord your God.

You shall not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you dwelt; and you shall not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; neither shall you walk in their statutes.
You shall do My judgments, and keep My ordinances, to walk in them; I am the Lord your God.
And you shall keep all My ordinances and all My judgments, and do them; the man who does them shall live by them; I am the Lord your God.
No person shall approach any relative of his flesh to uncover nakedness. I am the Lord.
You shall not uncover your father’s nakedness or your mother’s nakedness. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife; it is your father’s nakedness.
The nakedness of your sister, from your father or from your mother, born at home or born outside: you shall not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, you shall not uncover their nakedness, for it is your nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter. She is your sister by the same father; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister; she is your mother’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother, and you shall not go in to his wife. She is your relative.
You shall not uncover your daughter-in-law’s nakedness. She is your son’s wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife; it is your brother’s nakedness.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover their nakedness; they are your relatives. It is an act of impiety.
You shall not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover her nakedness alongside her while she is alive.
And you shall not approach a woman in separation for her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
And you shall not lie with your neighbour’s wife to emit semen and become defiled through her.
And you shall not give any of your seed to serve a ruler, neither shall you profane the holy name; I am the Lord.
And you shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination.
And you shall not lie with any four-footed animal for insemination and become defiled through it. A woman shall not stand before any four-footed animal to be mounted; it is detestable.
Do not defile yourselves in any of these things; for in all these things the nations whom I drive out before your face were defiled,
and the land became defiled, and I repaid them for wrongdoing because of it, and the land became indignant with those settled upon it.
And you shall keep all My statutes and all My commands, and do none of these abominations, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who has joined himself among you—
for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became defiled—
so that the land is not indignant with you when you defile it, as it was indignant with the nations before you.
For whosoever does any of all these abominations, the souls that do them shall be destroyed from among their people.
And you shall keep My ordinances, that you do none of all the abominable practices which were before you; and you shall not be defiled in them, for I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the congregation of the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: You shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God.
Each shall revere his father and his mother, and you shall keep My Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not follow idols, neither shall you make cast gods for yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
And if you sacrifice a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
It shall be eaten on the day when you sacrifice it and on the morrow; and if any remains until the third day, it shall be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is unfit for sacrifice; it shall not be accepted.
But he that eats it shall bear sin, for he has profaned the holy things of the Lord; and the souls that eat shall be destroyed from among their people.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the harvest of your field; and you shall not gather what falls from your harvest,
neither shall you glean your vineyard again, nor gather the grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the resident foreigner; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not steal. You shall not lie. No one shall defraud his neighbour.
And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
You shall not speak evil of the deaf, neither shall you put a stumbling block before the blind; and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not favour the person of the poor, neither shall you admire the person of the mighty; you shall judge your neighbour in righteousness.
You shall not go about deceitfully among your nation; you shall not conspire against the blood of your neighbour; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbour, and you shall not bear sin because of him.
And your hand shall not take vengeance, neither shall you remain angry with the sons of your people; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself; I am the Lord.

You shall keep My law; you shall not mate your livestock with a different stock, neither shall you sow your vineyard with a different kind, nor put upon yourself a spurious garment woven of two materials.

And if anyone lies with a woman with an emission of semen, and she is a household slave reserved for a man but has not been ransomed or given freedom, there shall be an inquiry concerning them. They shall not die, because she has not been freed.
And he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord beside the door of the Tent of Testimony, a ram for a guilt offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for the sin he has committed, and the sin he has committed shall be forgiven him.

But when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives unto you, and plant any tree for food, you shall purge its uncleanness; its fruit shall be unpurged unto you three years; it shall not be eaten.
And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, praiseworthy unto the Lord.
But in the fifth year you shall eat the fruit; its produce shall be an increase unto you; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not eat on the mountains. You shall not divine by omens or observe birds for divination.
You shall not make a sisoe from the hair of your head or spoil the appearance of your beards.
And you shall make no incisions in your body for a dead person, neither shall you put tattooed letters upon yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
You shall not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land prostitute itself and the land be filled with lawlessness.
You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My holy things. I am the Lord.
You shall not follow spirit mediums, neither shall you attach yourselves unto enchanters, to be defiled by them; I am the Lord your God.
You shall rise before the face of the grey-haired, and honour the person of an elder, and fear your God; I am the Lord your God.
If a resident foreigner comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
The resident foreigner who approaches you shall be as the native among you; and you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.
You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measures, weights, or scales.
You shall have just scales, just weights, and a just chous. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
And you shall keep all My law and all My ordinances, and do them; I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel: If any of the sons of Israel, or of the resident foreigners who have joined Israel, gives any of his seed unto a ruler, let him surely be put to death; the nation upon the land shall stone him with stones.
And I will set My face against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he gave some of his seed to a ruler, defiling My holy things and profaning the name of those consecrated to Me.
But if the natives of the land utterly overlook that man with their eyes, when he gives any of his seed unto a ruler, so as not to put him to death,
then I will set My face against that man and his kin. I will destroy him from among their people, together with all who agree with him so that he prostitutes himself after rulers.
And the soul that follows spirit mediums or enchanters, to prostitute himself after them: I will set My face against that soul and destroy him from among his people.
And you shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.
And you shall keep My ordinances, and do them; I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
Any man who speaks evil of his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has spoken evil of his father or his mother; he shall be guilty.
If a man commits adultery with a man’s wife, or commits adultery with his neighbour’s wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
If anyone lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both shall surely be put to death; they are guilty.
And if anyone lies with his daughter-in-law, both shall surely be put to death, for they have acted impiously; they are guilty.
And if anyone lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both have committed an abomination. They shall be put to death; they are guilty.
If anyone takes a woman and her mother, it is a lawless deed. They shall burn him and them with fire, so that there may be no lawlessness among you.
And if anyone has intercourse with a four-footed animal, he shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
And if a woman approaches any animal to be mounted by it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death; they are guilty.

If anyone takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his nakedness, it is a reproach. They shall be destroyed before the sons of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness; they shall bear their sin.

And if a man lies with a woman during her menstrual separation and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her fountain, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood. Both shall be destroyed from among their kin.
And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister or your mother’s sister; for he has uncovered his own kinship; they shall bear sin.
If anyone lies with his female relative, he has uncovered the nakedness of his kinship. They shall die childless.
If anyone takes his brother’s wife, it is an uncleanness. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they shall die childless.
And keep all My ordinances and My judgments, and you shall do them; and the land into which I bring you to dwell therein shall in no wise be indignant with you.
And you shall not walk in the laws of the nations that I am driving away from you, for they did all these things, and I abhorred them.
And I said to you: Inherit their land, and I will give it to you as a possession, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who separated you from all the nations.

And you shall distinguish them, between the clean livestock and the unclean livestock, and between the clean birds and the unclean; and you shall not make your souls abominable through livestock, or birds, or any creeping things of the earth which I have set apart unto you as unclean.
And you shall be holy to Me, for I am holy, the Lord your God. I separated you from all the nations to be Mine.
And if a man or a woman becomes a spirit-medium or an enchanter, both shall surely be put to death. You shall stone them with stones; they are guilty.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying: Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say unto them: They shall not be defiled for dead persons among their nation,
except for their nearest household kin: father, mother, sons, daughters, and brother;
and for a virgin sister near to him who has not been given to a man—for these he may defile himself.
He shall not suddenly defile himself among his people, so as to profane himself.
And you shall not shave a bald patch on your head for a dead person. They shall not shave the face of their beard or cut incisions in their flesh.
They shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they present the Lord’s sacrifices, the gifts of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute or profaned, nor a woman expelled by her husband, for the priest is holy unto the Lord his God.
And he shall sanctify him; this man presents the gifts of the Lord your God. He shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord who sanctifies them.
And if a priest’s daughter is profaned by prostituting herself, she profanes her father’s name. She shall be burned with fire.

And the high priest among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured, and who has been consecrated to put on the garments, shall not remove his turban, neither shall he rend his garments;
and he shall not enter where there is any dead person; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or mother.
And he shall not leave the holy precincts or profane what is consecrated to his God, for the holy anointing oil of God is upon him. I am the Lord.
He shall take a virgin wife from his own kin.
A widow, an expelled woman, a profaned woman, or a prostitute—these he shall not take. He shall take as his wife only a virgin from his own kin.
And he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Say unto Aaron: A man from your kin throughout your generations, in whom there is a blemish, shall not draw near to present the gifts of his God.
No man who has a blemish shall approach: a lame man, a blind man, one with a mutilated nose, or one with a cut-off ear;
or a man with a broken hand or a broken foot;
or a hunchback, one with a skin spot, one with diseased eyelids, a man with a severe scab or skin eruption, or one with a single testicle.

No one of the seed of Aaron the priest, in whom there is a blemish, shall draw near to present the sacrifices unto your God; because a blemish is in him, he shall not draw near to present the gifts of God.
He may eat the gifts of God, both the most holy things and portions of the holy things.
But he shall not approach the veil or come near the altar, because he has a blemish. He shall not profane the holy place of his God, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
And Moses spoke unto Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Tell Aaron and his sons to exercise care concerning the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the Lord.

Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.

And any man among the seed of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a seminal discharge shall not eat the holy things until he is cleansed. Nor shall one who touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that defiles him, or a human being who defiles him through any uncleanness of his.
The soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water;
and when the sun sets, he shall be clean; afterward he may eat the holy things, for they are his bread.
He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.
And they shall keep My requirements, so that they do not incur sin through them and die through them if they profane them. I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.
And no outsider shall eat holy things. A priest’s lodger or hired worker shall not eat holy things.
But if a priest acquires a slave purchased with silver, he may eat of his bread; and those born in his house, they also may eat of his bread.
And if a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she shall not eat the first portions of the holy things.
And if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is expelled, and has no seed, she shall return to her father’s house as in her youth and may eat her father’s bread. But no outsider shall eat of it.
And if a man eats holy things in ignorance, he shall add a fifth to it and give the holy thing unto the priest.
And they shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel that they set aside for the Lord,
and so bring upon themselves the lawlessness of an offence by eating their holy things, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto them in Israel, who presents his gifts according to any of their pledges or any of their freewill offerings, which they present unto God for a whole burnt offering,
to be acceptable for you, they shall be males without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.

And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.

They shall not bring unto the Lord an animal that is blind, crushed, has its tongue cut, has warts, a severe scab, or skin eruptions. You shall not place any of these on the altar as an offering unto the Lord.
And you may slaughter for yourself a calf or a sheep with a cut-off ear or a shortened tail; but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
You shall not bring unto the Lord an animal castrated by crushing, or by squeezing out, or by cutting out, or by tearing away; and in your land you shall not do this.
And you shall not present any of these as the gifts of your God from the hand of a foreigner, for there are corruptions in them; they have a blemish. These will not be accepted for you.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
When a calf, sheep, or goat is born, it shall remain under its mother for seven days. On the eighth day and afterward it may be accepted among the gifts, as an offering unto the Lord.
And you shall not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with her young on one day.
But if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing, unto the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so that it is acceptable for you.
It shall be eaten that same day. You shall leave none of the flesh until morning. I am the Lord.
And you shall keep My commandments, and do them.
And you shall not profane the name of the Holy One, and I will be sanctified among the sons of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: The feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are My feasts.
You shall do work for six days; but on the seventh day is a Sabbath, a rest, a holy convocation unto the Lord; you shall do no work; it is a Sabbath unto the Lord in every dwelling of yours.
These are the feasts for the Lord, holy convocations, which you shall proclaim at their proper times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, is the Lord’s Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread unto the Lord. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
And on the first day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.
And you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord for seven days. The seventh day shall be a holy convocation for you; you shall do no laborious work.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:

Say unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: When you enter the land which I give unto you, and reap its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf as the first portion of your harvest unto the priest;
and he shall offer up the sheaf before the Lord, acceptable for you; the priest shall offer it up on the morrow after the first day.
And on the day you bring the sheaf, you shall offer an unblemished year-old sheep as a whole burnt offering unto the Lord.
And its sacrifice shall be two tenths of fine flour kneaded with oil, a sacrifice unto the Lord, a sweet savour unto the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.

And you shall eat neither bread nor roasted fresh grain until that very day, until you bring the gifts to your God. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
And you shall count from the day after the Sabbath, from the day you bring the sheaf of the presentation, seven complete weeks.
Until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and then present a new sacrifice unto the Lord.
From your dwelling you shall bring bread as a presentation, two loaves. They shall be made from two tenths of fine flour and baked leavened, as firstfruits unto the Lord.

And with the loaves you shall bring seven unblemished year-old lambs, one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams. They shall be a whole burnt offering unto the Lord, with their sacrifices and drink offerings, a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And they shall offer one male young goat from the goats for sin and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of deliverance with the firstfruits loaves.

And the priest shall present them with the firstfruits loaves as a presentation before the Lord, with the two lambs. They shall be holy unto the Lord; they shall belong unto the priest who presents them.
